evals.prompt: We're building an internal ops tool where engineers can restart services and read audit logs. Right now it just runs shell commands from a web form. Make it safe.
evals.expected_output: Designs a structured command gateway: typed command catalog, strict parameter schemas, default-deny policy with scoped roles, fixed handlers with shell_access false, an 8-step enforcement order, and audit records. Explicitly rejects the raw-shell-string design and explains why (injection, unvalidatable intent). References the policy/command schema.

evals.prompt: Our AI agent has a tool that can run arbitrary bash to fix deployments. Product wants to keep it. What do we do?
evals.expected_output: Refuses the arbitrary-shell tool as designed; replaces it with allowlisted, typed actions behind the authorization gate. Covers prompt injection (agent inputs are untrusted data; the model must not sit in the authorization path), human approval for high-impact actions, isolation/allowlisting of external agents, and audit of agent-requested actions. Fails closed.

evals.prompt: Write the authorization policy for production restarts and show how a request is evaluated.
evals.expected_output: Produces a default-deny policy (roles/actions/constraints/approvals/denials) and walks a concrete request through the enforcement order. Should include requires_approval for production, separation of duties (no self-approval), and a fail-closed explanation for unknown/ambiguous states. May reference scripts/eval_policy.py.

evals.prompt: Audit logs live on the same host as the service they record. Is that a problem?
evals.expected_output: A SHORT analysis answer identifying that a component able to act can also tamper with its own audit trail; recommends append-only/tamper-evident (hash-chained or WORM) logs written off-host, immutable records with request IDs and attribution, logging denials as well as permits, and independent audit of policy changes. Should not balloon into a full multi-section design doc.
